high_consensus.description: Critical security/operability gap. Operator-added providers almost certainly require credentials, and without a contract teams will leak secrets into YAML or ad-hoc env vars. Highly actionable (naming, precedence, validation) with low implementation cost and high risk reduction.

High-value observability addition. Current debug tracing is insufficient for deprecation rollout decisions; aggregate counters are needed for objective sunset gating. Clear metrics and acceptance criteria can be added with moderate effort.

Critical spec conflict. Fail-closed startup and legacy compatibility requirements can produce contradictory behavior, especially with removed models. Must be resolved to avoid inconsistent enforcement and operator breakage.

Top-priority security concern. Partial-merge semantics can inadvertently bypass permission-elevation protections unless validation is explicitly defined on merged results. Clear, actionable, and high-risk if omitted.

disputed.description: Reasonable nice-to-have, but projected per-invocation cost is hard to estimate reliably at resolution time without token forecasts. Benefit is real for operator safety, yet implementation complexity and false confidence trade-offs are non-trivial.

blockers.concern: Core design is still blocked by unresolved deferred decisions (DD-1..DD-6) with fallback defaults that may be wrong.
blockers.why_matters: If implementation starts with fallback assumptions (permissions strategy, override semantics, startup-hook language), architecture can lock into incompatible behavior and require rework across all 4 sprints.
blockers.location: Scope & Prioritization -> Deferred decisions to resolve before Sprint 1
blockers.recommendation: Do not start Sprint 1 coding until DD-1..DD-6 are formally ratified in SDD; add a hard go/no-go checklist and explicit impact analysis for each fallback path.

blockers.concern: Endpoint security controls still have TOCTOU and parsing edge risks (IPv6 literals, IDN/punycode, connection reuse, proxy behavior).
blockers.why_matters: A single bypass in URL/DNS validation can turn operator-configurable endpoints into SSRF or internal network access, which is a project-stopping security incident.
blockers.recommendation: Define a single hardened URL/IP validation library used by all runtimes, include IPv6/IDN/proxy test vectors, and add outbound network policy enforcement at runtime host level.

blockers.concern: Hybrid Bridgebuilder model (build-time defaults + runtime overlay) risks divergence between TS runtime and global resolver behavior.
blockers.why_matters: If Bridgebuilder computes truncation/resolution differently from core resolver, users will see skill-specific inconsistencies that are hard to debug and undermine SoT guarantees.
blockers.location: FR-1.1, Technical Considerations -> Hybrid Bridgebuilder pattern
blockers.recommendation: Extract one shared resolution library and one shared schema contract used by both core and Bridgebuilder; prohibit duplicate resolver logic.

blockers.concern: Locking strategy assumes reliable flock semantics and local filesystem behavior that may not hold in all environments.
blockers.why_matters: On NFS/containerized/shared volumes, lock behavior can be inconsistent, causing startup hangs, stale reads, or repeated fail-closed outages.
blockers.recommendation: Specify supported filesystem/runtime environments, add lock timeout and recovery semantics, and test under container + network filesystem scenarios.

blockers.concern: Resolution logic remains highly complex due to coexistence of new shape, legacy shapes, tier mappings, aliases, and optional prefer_pro overlay.
blockers.why_matters: Even with precedence rules, combinatorial interactions can produce edge-case misrouting in production that tests miss, especially during phased migration where mixed configs are expected.
blockers.recommendation: Add a compatibility matrix with explicit supported combinations and unsupported states; enforce migration guardrails that reduce simultaneous active paths per skill.

blockers.concern: Writing and sourcing '.run/merged-model-aliases.sh' creates a shell-code injection surface if escaping is imperfect.
blockers.why_matters: Any serialization bug can execute arbitrary shell when adapters source the file, turning config parsing defects into command execution.
blockers.recommendation: Avoid executable shell serialization; use a non-executable data format (JSON) plus strict parser, or generate shell with a formally verified escaping function and fuzz tests.
